claims.text: Hypertensive crises before or during surgery: nitroprusside infusion
claims.quote: Nitroprusside can be infused for hypertensive crises preoperatively or intraoperatively.

claims.text: During surgery: hypertensive paroxysms → phentolamine IV or nitroprusside infusion; tachyarrhythmias → propranolol or esmolol
claims.quote: During surgery, paroxysms of hypertension should be controlled with injections of phentolamine 1 to 5 mg IV or nitroprusside infusion (2 to 4 mcg/kg/minute), and tachyarrhythmias should be controlled with propranolol or esmolol.
Metastatic pheochromocytoma should be treated with alpha-blockers and beta-blockers.

claims.text: metyrosine (tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor) may lower catecholamine production when BP is hard to control; not readily available
claims.quote: Metyrosine, a tyrosine hydroxylase inhibitor, may be used to decrease catecholamine production in patients whose blood pressure is difficult to control but is not readily available.

claims.text: Bilateral adrenalectomy: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV twice a day before and during surgery (avoids acute glucocorticoid insufficiency)
claims.quote: sufficient hydrocortisone (100 mg IV twice a day) given before and during surgery avoids acute glucocorticoid insufficiency due to bilateral adrenalectomy
